items.name: cn
items.description: Class-name composer: merges conditional classes and resolves conflicting Tailwind utilities so a consumer's className always wins over a component's defaults.

items.name: motion
items.description: The three timings this library animates at, as class-name constants: motionMicro (interaction feedback), motionStandard (a surface arriving or leaving) and motionDeliberate (an unfolding). The property list stays at the call site because Tailwind compiles the class names it finds by scanning source text — a recipe that interpolated `transition-[${properties}]` would generate no rule and the element would silently not animate. Written after the same duration/easing pair was hand-assembled fifty times, which also revealed that the library uses --ui-ease-out in fifty cases out of fifty while the token layer offers four easings and four --ui-motion-* intents with no consumers at all.

items.name: fade-ramp
items.description: The perceptual edge ramp every fade paints or masks with: a Gaussian penumbra (the cumulative normal, mean 0.55, sigma 0.22 of the depth) sampled at seventeen stops, so there is no corner at either end for the eye to read as a stripe, with a second table for dark grounds that leaves the same perceptual fraction of ink visible (light ink under a dark veil stays visible longer at equal alpha; the correction is the polarity's and agrees to ±0.015 across role pairs). paintRamp(direction, ground) builds the painted gradient, switching per stop with light-dark(); maskRamp(direction, depth) builds its complement for mask-image. The tables ship as numbers; fade-ramp.test.ts re-derives them from the curve and the OKLab model.

items.name: viz
items.description: The data-visualisation maths layer (ADR 0023): pure functions that turn numbers into numbers and SVG path strings — extent, a linear scale that draws a flat series as a level line, evenly spaced series points inside a plot's insets, line and area paths, columns that always stand on zero with their data end rounded and negatives hanging below it, and Intl number formatting. Every coordinate is rounded to two decimals so server and client write identical paths. Imports no maths module yet; d3 modules are admitted behind this file when a chart needs band or time scales, and never reach a public signature.

items.name: chrome-control
items.description: The 32px chrome control: a square, softly-rounded button filled with --ui-bg-elevated and carrying no edge. Not a Button variant — every button type is either a fill with a matching edge or an edge on nothing, and this is the one shape that is a fill with no edge at all. It belongs to page chrome (a menu toggle, a back arrow, a calendar's month arrows) rather than to the action vocabulary. Exported as one recipe because it was independently reinvented four times before it had a name.

items.name: menu-surface
items.description: The menu surface: one panel recipe and one row recipe, shared by Menu and ContextMenu. Not two components that happen to look alike — Base UI's ContextMenu re-exports Menu's Item, Group, Separator and Submenu verbatim, so they are literally the same rows in the same popup, differing only in what opens them. A recipe rather than a component for the same reason chrome-control is: it styles, it does not wrap, so the behaviour layer keeps ownership of roles, roving focus, typeahead and dismissal.

items.name: compose-event-handlers
items.description: Composes a consumer event handler with component-owned behaviour. The consumer runs first and may prevent optional internal behaviour with preventDefault; non-cancellable safety invariants stay outside the helper.

items.name: fx
items.description: The effects layer's CSS materials and its vocabulary (ADR 0022): glass (with edge, inner and specular), grain, sheen, glow, shimmer and ink, applied as a class on a component's ROOT through the typed fx() helper — <Card className={fx("glass", "edge")}> — and reaching the part they paint through data-slot, so no component grows a prop. One stylesheet per effect under styles/fx/, imported through fx.css after Tailwind and the theme, all inside `@layer fx` so an effect outranks a component's utilities while the app's unlayered CSS still outranks the effect. Glass paints --ui-bg-glass, a tint the resolver derives per brand and scheme so primary and muted ink clear AA over anything behind it (needs a theme emitted with the glass pair — theme zero's stylesheet carries it). The floor of every effect is the component: reduced transparency, forced colours and reduced motion hand each property back with revert-layer. EFFECTS is the single source of what exists, what each is for and where it applies; check:fx holds the stylesheets to it. The two shader effects, aurora and halo, are named here and shipped by the optional `shader` item. sweep(element) plays sheen's one-shot pass of light.

items.name: shader
items.description: The OPTIONAL shader runtime of the effects layer (ADR 0022): aurora (the brand colour moving through a fill or a ground) and halo (light travelling round a surface that works or listens). startShaders() — server-safe, reference-counted, returns its stop function — finds every .fx-aurora / .fx-halo root, mounts one canvas in the part the effect paints and draws it from tokens read where that part sits, through ONE shared WebGL2 context. A shader is admitted only if it paints pixels it owns, takes every input from a token, keeps the component as its floor and guards the contrast of the ink on its part per pixel; check:fx enforces the first two on the sources. The canvas draws the part's own rounded shape (iOS Safari drops a CSS clip on an animating canvas), covers the border box, sits under the part's content or directly after a track's fill so a Slider's thumb stays on top, and follows the component's own state transitions through registered properties (--ui-fx-on, --ui-fx-halo-strength). State is published on the root as data-fx-aurora / data-fx-halo (live, still, floor, lost, unsupported); reduced motion draws one chosen still frame and the loop sleeps when nothing moves. configureShaders() and sampleShader() exist for stories and contrast tests.

items.name: use-controllable-state
items.description: The one implementation of the controlled/uncontrolled pattern (CONVENTIONS §4). Returns [value, setValue] with a referentially stable setter; a controlled component never updates its own state, and switching modes mid-life warns in development instead of silently picking a winner.

items.name: use-is-stuck
items.description: Is a position: sticky element currently parked at its offset? The state a pinned bar changes appearance on, and the one CSS cannot answer — there is no :stuck. OBSERVED rather than listened for: an IntersectionObserver at threshold 1, with a root margin pulled in by the caller's own sticky offset plus a pixel, rooted at the nearest SCROLLING ancestor rather than the viewport — a bar pinned inside a scrolling panel sits at a fixed viewport position, so a viewport-rooted observer watches it never move and the state never flips. No sentinel node, no scroll listener, and no per-frame getBoundingClientRect, which is a forced synchronous layout on the busiest thread there is. Header's own affix state is the first consumer; Fade's visibility on a pinned bar is the second.

items.name: use-scroll-edges
items.description: Where a scroll container currently sits between its ends, on both axes — the state a Fade binds its isVisible to, since a ramp at an edge means there is more content that way. A passive scroll listener rather than an observer, deliberately: the question is the offset itself rather than a boolean, and the IntersectionObserver equivalent needs a sentinel node pinned at every edge. Paired with a ResizeObserver for the container AND a commit-time re-measure, because content appended to an already-full list resizes nothing and a ResizeObserver alone never fires. Takes the absolute value of the inline offset, since an RTL container scrolls to a negative scrollLeft.

items.name: font-aspekta
items.description: Aspekta Variable — the design system's single typeface (SIL OFL 1.1, by Ivo Dolenc). Installs the @font-face CSS and the OFL license text; the ~30KB variable woff2 (weight 100-900) is binary and is fetched from the repo with the one-line curl documented at the top of aspekta.css, into the same directory. Keep OFL.txt with the font wherever it is deployed. Preload the woff2 (<link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin> — snippet at the top of aspekta.css) so font-display: swap does not flash the fallback face on first paint.

items.name: combobox
items.description: An editable text field with a filtered listbox: one committed value, free text allowed, options in labelled groups, rows that can be links, async loading/empty/error states, and an action row that is always present. Focus never leaves the input — the highlight is an aria-activedescendant. The field is Input's control and the panel and rows are Select's; the ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern comes from the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012), wrapped so no third-party type reaches a public prop signature.

items.name: media-toggle
items.description: The pause/play control WCAG 2.2.2 requires for video that plays on its own (#36). A round chrome control on the media family (--ui-bg-media, --ui-text-on-media), so it reads the same over the video in both schemes. Drives the media element it is given and follows its play/pause events; starts paused under prefers-reduced-motion. Both accessible names are required props.

items.name: theme-zero-css
items.description: Theme zero as a stylesheet: the --ui-* token layer (light and dark, following prefers-color-scheme) plus the Tailwind v4 @theme block that maps every utility the components use onto it. The install path that works without npm (issue #30) — generated from @bydiorama/tokens' toTailwindTheme() and toCss(), the same output Storybook renders against, and kept fresh by `pnpm check:theme-css`. Import it once after `@import "tailwindcss";`. A brand theme is not this file: run the emitters (resolveThemePair → toCss) with the brand's seed instead.

items.name: button
items.description: The primary action control. Five variants (primary, secondary, outline, ghost, danger), three sizes (44/32/24px), pill or rounded, plus icon-only and full-width forms. Icon-only buttons require an aria-label at the type level. isBusy keeps focus but swallows activation (the double-submit guard), unlike isDisabled, which leaves the tab order. `render` makes it a link (or the router's Link) with every state intact; `buttonClassName()` is the same recipe for markup React does not own.

items.name: header
items.description: The page's top bar: leading controls, an optional row of navigation items, trailing controls. A <header> so it is the banner landmark, but deliberately NOT a nav — the bar also holds a brand mark that links home and an avatar that opens the account menu, and calling all of that navigation would make the landmark useless to skip to; the item row names itself. Header.MenuButton opens ONE of two surfaces, chosen by the layout rather than by a prop: a Menu on desktop, and below the breakpoint a Sheet carrying the whole Sidebar, which is removed rather than narrowed. A nav item's current state takes the third step of a four-step fill ramp, because hover and current shared one fill until they were drawn side by side. An item is a real <a> when given an href and a <button> otherwise, because the design draws two carrying a chevron that open menus rather than navigate.

items.name: site-header
items.description: The SITE header (#33) — a wordmark, a short row of quiet links and one call to action — composed from Header, which stays app chrome. Data-driven (brand, items, cta) rather than compound, because an Astro page cannot compose Header's parts across the island boundary. Below the caller's collapseBelow point the bar keeps two words, the wordmark and a text Menu control, and the menu is a full-screen Sheet from the top with the CTA at its foot; the switch is a scoped media query, so the desktop bar is static-safe HTML. isOverMedia puts the bar on the hero with the media inks and a 64% --ui-bg-media scrim until the page scrolls under it.

items.name: input
items.description: Single-line text field with its label, helper text and error message as one accessible unit. Three sizes (48/40/32px), leading and trailing slots. The label prop is required by the type system — a placeholder is not a label. errorText wires aria-invalid and aria-describedby together so the two cannot drift apart.

items.name: popover
items.description: A panel anchored to a trigger, for secondary content that should not take over the page. Compound: Trigger, Panel, Title, Description, Close. Positioning, focus restoration, dismissal and ARIA wiring come from Base UI (ADR 0012), wrapped so no third-party type reaches a public prop signature. Bare text inside the 32px-radius panel is inset one step; boxed children sit flush.

items.name: toast
items.description: A transient notification stacked bottom-right of the viewport, built on Base UI Toast. One Provider + Viewport around the app; everything fires through useToast() (add, close, update, promise). Five types carried by a leading intent glyph — the surface never tints. Toasts collapse into a stack of three, clamped to the frontmost height, and expand on viewport hover or focus. The viewport landmark label and the close button's accessible name are required at the type level.

items.name: tooltip
items.description: A short label that appears on hover or focus and names a control that cannot name itself. Compound: Provider, Trigger, Content. The smallest surface in the library and the only one that is never interactive — a pointer leaving the trigger dismisses it, so nothing inside could be reached. An opaque --ui-bg-emphasis chip rather than an elevated panel, because a tooltip and a Popover are told apart by their fill before anything else. Anchoring, the hover and focus wiring, the delay group and aria-describedby come from Base UI (ADR 0012).

items.name: modal
items.description: A dialog that takes over the page: scrim behind, focus trapped inside, focus restored to the trigger on close. Compound: Trigger, Surface, Title, Description, Footer, Close. Always modal — a non-modal dialog with a scrim is a Popover. Dismissal by Escape and scrim-click is on by default and can be turned off for unsaved work. Built on the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012), wrapped so no third-party type reaches a public prop signature.

items.name: multiselect
items.description: A filterable list of options where more than one can be chosen, with the selection shown as removable chips. Listbox/combobox ARIA, aria-multiselectable, active-descendant management, typeahead, filtering and dismissal all come from the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012), wrapped so no third-party type reaches a public prop signature. The trigger reuses Input's control surface; chips are Badge components with real remove buttons.

items.name: select
items.description: Choose ONE value from a list. The trigger is Input's control surface, exactly as Multiselect's is — a field is a field, and three components inventing three variants of the same box is how a system stops looking like one. Listbox ARIA, typeahead, roving focus and dismissal come from the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012), wrapped so no third-party type reaches a public prop signature.

items.name: avatar
items.description: A person or entity as a photo or their initials. Circle or rounded, three sizes. `name` is required in both forms — it is the image's alt text and the source of the initials. Initials are aria-hidden and the full name exposed separately, so a screen reader announces the person rather than spelling out letters.

items.name: badge
items.description: A short status or selection label. Six variants (selected, unselected, neutral, success, warning, danger), two sizes, pill or rounded, with an optional trailing slot. Renders a span and takes no interaction props: anything actionable is a real button passed into iconEnd, keeping the accessible name at the call site.

items.name: banner
items.description: An inline message attached to the surface it belongs to — not a toast, not a dialog. Five intents (neutral, info, success, warning, danger), an optional leading glyph slot and an optional dismiss control whose accessible name is required at the type level. Announces only when isLive is set, so a banner rendered with the page does not talk over the user. Composes inside a Popover panel as a boxed child.

items.name: card
items.description: A titled surface that groups related controls. Renders a <section> with a real heading at a caller-chosen level, so a card is navigable structure rather than a styled div. Compound: Header (with an actions slot) and Footer, both carrying the unboxed inset while boxed children sit flush. The surface is deliberately identical to Popover's panel.

items.name: calendar
items.description: A month grid for picking one date, with month and year selects in its header. Ours rather than a library's (ADR 0012): the hard parts are the ARIA grid and the keyboard contract, and both are decisions this system has to own. One roving tab stop, arrows by day and week, Home/End across the week, PageUp/PageDown by month, and an arrow that walks off the edge carries the grid with it. The two header selects replace the grid in place at its own height, so the card never resizes; each is a listbox with its own roving stop and returns focus to its trigger. Month and weekday names come from Intl, so a consumer in another locale gets their own without this library shipping a translation table. Unavailable dates use aria-disabled and stay focusable — a date a screen-reader user cannot reach is one they cannot be told the reason for.

items.name: menu
items.description: A list of commands, opened from a trigger. The whole ARIA menu contract — role=menu and menuitem, roving focus, typeahead, Escape and outside-press dismissal, submenu timing and the aria-haspopup/aria-expanded wiring — comes from the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012), wrapped so no third-party type reaches a public prop signature. Its panel and rows come from the shared menu surface, which ContextMenu draws from the same recipe, so the two cannot drift apart. Item.onSelect is named for the verb rather than for the pointer, because a menu row is chosen by keyboard as often as by mouse.

items.name: context-menu
items.description: The same menu, opened by a right-click on a region rather than by a button. Only three parts live here — Root, Trigger and Panel — because Base UI's ContextMenu re-exports Menu's Item, Group, Separator and Submenu verbatim; duplicating them would create two drawings of one surface. Requires the `menu` item for its rows. The keyboard path matters more here than anywhere else in the library: a surface that only opens on right-click is unreachable without a pointer, so Base UI opens it on Shift+F10 and the context-menu key as well.

items.name: date-picker
items.description: A date field that opens a Calendar. Two things this system already owns, composed: the field is Input's control surface — a field is a field — and the panel is the Calendar card itself rather than a second surface wrapped around one. Choosing a date closes the panel; clearing it deliberately does not, because the next thing that user wants is another date. Anchoring, dismissal and focus restoration come from Base UI (ADR 0012), wrapped so no third-party type reaches a public prop signature. The value is formatted with Intl by default and formatValue is the call-site escape hatch, so no date library ships with it.

items.name: card-sorting
items.description: A reorderable list of cards, with a grip on each row. Reordering works three ways and all three are first-class: a pointer drag, a keyboard lift-and-move (Space to lift, arrows to move, Escape to put it back), and a no-drag pointer path of click-to-lift then click-to-place, which is what WCAG 2.5.7 requires. Every path goes through one move and one polite live region that announces the row's name, its new position and the list's. Built without a drag library (ADR 0012) — the accessible half of this pattern is the half a drag library does not solve.

items.name: checkbox
items.description: A binary choice with its label as one control. Supports the mixed/indeterminate state for a parent whose children are partly selected. The whole row is the 24px target; the painted box stays 18px. Controlled or uncontrolled through the shared useControllableState hook.

items.name: radio
items.description: One choice from a set that stays visible. Compound: RadioGroup owns the legend, the shared name, the selection and the error; Radio is one option. A real fieldset around real radio inputs, so arrow-key navigation, the single tab stop, form participation and the legend-as-part-of-the-name all come from the platform rather than from ARIA. Checkbox's geometry with a circle and a dot: an 18px control on a 1px edge, a 24px row.

items.name: switch
items.description: A control that takes effect immediately, unlike a Checkbox, which states an intention the surrounding form later submits. A native input with role=switch, so it is announced as on/off rather than checked. The whole row is the 24px target; the track stays 36x20. Controlled or uncontrolled through the shared useControllableState hook.

items.name: sparkline
items.description: An inline, axis-free trend in one of the eight categorical data slots — line, area or columns, at the sheet's 160×40 or 120×32. One image to assistive technology (role=img), named by a required label and described by a required, person-written description: the one chart allowed to ship without a data table (ADR 0023 §4). Server-safe and deterministic; ships no handlers.

items.name: chart
items.description: Bars (grouped or stacked), lines and areas on a nice-tick value axis, in a figure that always carries its title, a person-written takeaway, a shape-and-colour legend for two or more series, and a view-as-table toggle backed by Table. The plot is one tab stop: arrow keys walk categories and series, each move is announced politely, and a tooltip follows the pointer and the keyboard. BarChart, LineChart and AreaChart are thin presets over Chart with Chart.Bars / .Lines / .Areas / .Rule children. Eight ordinal slots, never cycled; solid strokes only.

items.name: stat-tiles
items.description: The first block: a row of headline numbers in one surface frame, tiles separated by hairlines. Each tile is a label, a figure at the fixed --ui-text-figure role, a change line whose glyph says which way and whose colour says whether that is good (polarity: up-is-good by default, down-is-good for costs), and an optional Sparkline element. A <dl>; loading, no-value and no-comparison states keep the tile. Formats and computes nothing. Also exports StatDelta and StatFigure, the change line and a figure-plus-change row.

items.name: chart-card
items.description: The Chart frame with a stat tile's figure and change under its title, so the card says how much, and whether that is good, before the plot is read. The description stays required and stays the chart's accessible description; it is no longer printed. By default one fading area (Chart.Areas wash="fade"); any Chart mark goes in as children. Below the head it is the Chart, untouched.

items.name: meter
items.description: One value against a range — a gauge, not a task. An 8px bar or the sheet's 80px ring with role=meter, the clamped value and an aria-valuetext equal to the printed reading. Warning and danger states require their own words (the type enforces it), a target is a solid rule that requires its label, and no reading requires emptyText rather than an invented zero. Server-safe; ships no handlers.

items.name: progress
items.description: A determinate progress bar with an optional label and percentage, in two track heights (16/8px). A div with role=progressbar and the three ARIA value attributes, because unlike a checkbox or a button a progress bar has no native behaviour to inherit. The value is clamped and the clamped value is what is announced.

items.name: sidebar
items.description: The primary navigation rail, built from ROWS rather than links: a row becomes an <a> when given an href and is otherwise a plain slot, because the design puts a search field in one and a progress bar in another. Sections carry the second level, optionally collapsible, at the same inset — hierarchy is type and colour, not indentation. The current page is announced through aria-current rather than fill alone. First consumer of the --ui-nav-* role family, so a themed portal re-skins its chrome by re-binding six roles. No roving tabindex and no menu roles — navigation is links, and the browser's own contract is worth more than arrow keys.

items.name: nav-rail
items.description: The navigation rail at its narrow width: 48px, one icon per row. A SIBLING of Sidebar rather than a mode of it — six of Sidebar's ten parts change what they MEAN at this width rather than what they measure, which is the same test CONVENTIONS §7a already uses to split Sheet from Drawer (ADR 0015). The one-line difference: at full width a row is a slot, at rail width a row is a control, so a row is an <a> when it navigates and a <button> when it acts and never a container. Both the icon and the label are REQUIRED types, because the label is invisible and there is no text to fall back to. Sidebar's first level survives as a named group with a hairline, since a label-plus-chevron disclosure cannot exist at this width. The current row carries a 2px marker as well as aria-current: --ui-nav-active-bg is the family's only fill, so hover and current would otherwise paint the same square. Shares the --ui-nav-* family and the row lane with Sidebar, so a layout can swap one for the other without the navigation moving or changing colour.

items.name: drawer
items.description: A panel that comes up from the bottom and is dismissed by dragging it down. Distinct from Sheet, and the distinction is the GESTURE rather than the geometry: a Sheet is anchored to a side edge and dismissed by scrim or Escape, while a Drawer carries a handle, follows the finger, and closes past a distance or velocity threshold. Base UI supplies the focus trap, scroll lock, Escape and focus restoration (ADR 0012); the drag is ours, with no drag library in the dependency list. The handle is a real button as well as a drag target, which is the single-pointer alternative WCAG 2.5.7 requires.

items.name: sheet
items.description: A panel anchored to the left or right edge of the viewport, full height, over a scrim — the surface a narrow screen uses for what a wide one keeps docked: the navigation rail, a filter set, a record edited beside the page. Third component on the Base UI behaviour layer, deliberately Modal's shape because the focus trap, scroll lock, Escape and focus restoration are the same problem; only the panel's position differs. Four optional regions — a 48px chrome band, a Title, a Body and a stacked footer — of which only the Body scrolls, so the band and the action row stay put and each gains a hairline once there is content behind it. Three width CAPS on tokens that already existed: sm is the rail's own width and the default, md and lg are Modal's two dialog widths. A third side, top, is the full-screen variant a site's collapsed menu uses: flush on every edge, uncapped. The two INNER corners are rounded so it reads as a drawer rather than a modal, and there is no side of 'bottom' — that is Drawer, whose contract is the gesture.

items.name: slider
items.description: A single-value slider in three shapes: a track in four heights (8/16/24/32px) with a gradient fill, optional stepper buttons and a slot for a value control; an inline bar (32/40/48px) with the label and value inside it, for dense panels; and a balance slider whose fill grows from an origin toward the thumb between two named poles. formatValue is shown and announced as one. Pointer capture, keyboard stepping, Home/End, RTL and touch come from the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012), wrapped so no third-party type reaches a public prop signature — the value is a number, never an array. The control is padded to a 24px target even when the painted track is 8px; the thumb carries SC 1.4.11 with a ring floored at 3:1, and its focus ring keys off the input inside it.

items.name: range-slider
items.description: Two thumbs on one track; the fill is the span between them — a filter for 'from what, to what'. Everything visible is Slider's, read from Slider's own geometry table, while three things differ: the value is a readonly [number, number] tuple, each thumb is its own native input with its own required name (startThumbLabel / endThumbLabel), and the thumbs may meet but never cross — a dragged thumb stops at the other rather than pushing it. The readout states both ends with an en dash and is on by default. Base UI Slider underneath (ADR 0012).

items.name: tabs
items.description: A segmented control that switches which panel is shown. Compound: List, Tab, Panel. Roving tabindex, arrow navigation, Home/End and the two-way tab-to-panel ARIA pairing come from the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012), wrapped so no third-party type reaches a public prop signature. Activation is manual: arrows move focus, Enter or Space selects.

items.name: accordion
items.description: A list of disclosures. Compound: Item, Trigger, Panel. Single-open by default with an isMultiple switch, a plain and a card variant, and a panel whose height animates from the content it actually holds — so it can carry form controls rather than only copy. Each trigger is a real button inside a real heading at a heading level you choose, so the list is navigable by heading. Roving focus, open-state ARIA and the height measurement come from the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012), wrapped so no third-party type reaches a public prop signature.

items.name: textarea
items.description: Multi-line text field with its label, helper text and error message as one accessible unit. The control surface is Input's, so the two stack in a form without a seam; height comes from the native rows attribute and grows with a vertical drag. The label prop is required by the type system — a placeholder is not a label. errorText wires aria-invalid and aria-describedby together so the two cannot drift apart.

items.name: aspect-ratio
items.description: A media frame whose height comes from its width. Six named ratios from the sheet — square, story, portrait, landscape, card, screen — over a recessed well, clipped to the soft radius. A child is sized and cropped from the outside, so the call site is just src and alt. The vocabulary is closed on purpose: 'story' means the same shape wherever it is written, and nobody has to remember which way round 9/16 goes.

items.name: image-overlay
items.description: A picture with content on top of it. `scrim` darkens the bottom edge and holds a caption; `full` covers the frame, blurs it and centres an action. It IS an AspectRatio frame rather than a copy of one. The veil's strength is a conformance floor, not a taste setting: it is the point at which the caption's inks clear AA over the brightest possible photograph, which is the only guarantee a component putting text on unknown images can make.

items.name: thumbnail
items.description: A 48px attachment tile with an optional remove control on its corner — 16px of paint, 24px of target, revealed on hover AND on focus so a keyboard user is not tabbing to something invisible. Thumbnail.Group lays several out as a spaced row or as an overlapping stack that spreads back out on hover, with an overflow counter. removeLabel is required by the type whenever onRemove is passed: a cross with no accessible name announces as 'button'.

items.name: image-upload
items.description: A form field whose control is a drop target. Four states — empty, busy, attached, rejected — plus a drag-over state the component owns. Built on a real <input type="file">, so the keyboard path is the native picker rather than a re-implementation, and `browse` is a real button rather than the sheet's styled text. ImageUpload.File is one row mid-upload, drawn with a real Progress so its fill stays on the legible accent; ImageUpload.Grid and .Add are the multiple-image layout. errorText is what puts the field in `rejected`, so the message and the state cannot disagree.

items.name: image-edit
items.description: A crop stage with zoom and optional rotation. The crop WINDOW is fixed and the image moves behind it — by drag, and by the arrow keys, which the sheet draws no path for at all. Rectangular or circular; the circle is the avatar case, where the mask matches the destination and corner marks are deliberately absent. The stage is painted with the media ground rather than --ui-bg-emphasis, which IS the accent and would turn an image editor's stage into the brand colour. It is the body of a dialog, not the dialog: the caller wraps it in Modal and supplies the title, the close and the footer.

items.name: skeleton
items.description: A placeholder standing in for content that has not arrived. One element, no variants, sized entirely from the outside with className — the same shape as shadcn/ui's Skeleton, so a consumer's intuition transfers, and deliberately not a vocabulary: a `lines` or `variant` prop only re-describes the layout the skeleton is standing in for, and that layout is already written beside it. Defaults to a full-width bar at body height so a bare <Skeleton /> is visible rather than a 0px box, fills with the same recessed well Table's own loading bars use, and pulses under motion-safe. aria-hidden by default — the announcement belongs on the region that is loading, as aria-busy, which only the caller can place.

items.name: dot-pattern
items.description: A decorative dot-grid layer for canvas grounds — the texture behind the Creative Editor stage and the Library's business-card previews. One aria-hidden SVG that fills its container absolutely and paints evenly spaced circular dots, nothing else: no ground of its own, no edge, no pointer target. Geometry defaults transcribe the shipped Paper shader recipe (2px dots on a 16px pitch) and are plain-number props (gap, dotSize); the dot ink is border-subtle carried as currentColor, so className retints it with any ink utility, and the caller's container keeps its own background showing through between the dots. Paper draws this with a WebGL shader; the tiled-SVG rendering is the same geometry with no runtime dependency, crisp at any DPR and printable.

items.name: fade
items.description: An edge fade — the gradient that dissolves overflowing content into the ground it sits on, signalling continuation: under a pinned header, above a composer bar, at the cut of a truncated preview. One aria-hidden span, absolutely pinned to one edge of the caller's clipping container, painting a perceptual ramp (fade-ramp: a Gaussian penumbra with a dark-scheme correction) in the container's own bg role, so there is no start line or stripe for the eye to catch. side (top/bottom/left/right), size (24/48/96 on the spacing scale) and ground (base/surface/elevated/sunken, or affix under a translucent pinned bar, where the ramp ends at the bar's own alpha) are the parameters. isVisible gates it by opacity on the motion tokens; scrollContainer binds it to a scroller, easing it out over the last band-depth of scroll instead of switching off at the end and insetting it off a classic scrollbar. It is paint, never a participant: pointer-events none, no children, no interactive targets in the band, and every faded region pairs with a caller-composed route to the full content. fadeMask is the ground-agnostic complement for containers whose ground is not a role.

items.name: empty-state
items.description: The absence of content, explained: a mark on a 32px well, a sentence saying what is missing, a second saying why, and the control that fixes it. Every part but the title is optional and the action is a real Button, rendered exactly as passed. It announces nothing on its own — a container that swaps it in for content the reader was looking at owns that decision, which is why Table marks the cell it renders this into aria-live.

items.name: table
items.description: A data surface built from hairlines, not fills. A real <table> with fixed lanes and one flexing column, three densities, sortable headers that report rather than sort, row selection whose labels the type requires, and loading and empty bodies that keep the header and the lane widths. Nothing inside the frame carries a radius — the frame clips, which lands on the concentric inner corner without writing a value the radius scale does not have.

items.name: chat-composer
items.description: The message box of the agent chat: one frame holding an attachment tray, an auto-growing text region and a control row. A compact pill at rest, squaring to radius-xl the moment the text wraps — the layout switch is measured from the rendered line boxes, not declared, because a composer cannot know in advance whether a sentence will wrap. Send carries the state of the conversation: disabled while the field is blank, accent when sendable, and an inverse-filled Stop while the agent answers. Enter submits, Shift+Enter opens a line, and an Enter committing an IME candidate does neither.

items.name: chat-message
items.description: The two voices of an agent thread, deliberately asymmetric. The sender sits in a right-aligned bg-elevated bubble capped at a share of the column, with attachments inside it and delivery state carried by a caption — the bubble's fill never moves. The receiver owns the full width with no bubble at all and a looser leading, a static caret while streaming, a ghost actions row revealed on hover AND on focus, and a failure block that stays attached to the turn instead of floating off as a toast. One item, two components: there is no bare <ChatMessage>, because the receiver has no bubble and a role prop would give it one.

items.name: chat-progress
items.description: What the agent shows between the question and the answer. Four escalating forms on ONE axis — thinking, activity, steps, measured — discriminated by `form`, so a step list with no steps and a bar with no value are compile errors rather than empty boxes. Every form folds to the same receipt row when the work finishes and re-expands from it, because the log is history rather than chrome; a stopped run replaces the form with a failure line and keeps the log above it. role="status", polite. The measured form is the Progress primitive, and the spinner is CSS — griddy has no spinner glyph and a private SVG is not the answer.

items.name: chat-widget
items.description: The artifact container — the thing the agent hands you to take away. One shell with two payload families: TEXT (a header naming the artifact, prose capped at 320px behind a fade, a Copy/Edit bar) and MEDIA (a stage at a fixed ratio, an optional frame rail and caption, an Edit/Download bar). One component because the container, the action bar and the dark treatment are identical across both. bg-elevated, radius-lg, an 8px inset and NO border — the fill alone is the boundary, and the media's radius-md is concentric with it by construction. The body becomes a named, focusable region only WHILE it scrolls, so a short draft puts no tab stop in front of the reader.

items.name: chat-questionnaire
items.description: The agent asking, inside the thread: a question followed by tappable options — text rows or image tiles. Single-select commits on tap; multi-select collects and confirms; answering collapses it to a receipt where the question stays and the answer becomes a selected Badge. It has NO container, no fill and no action bar, which is why it is not a ChatWidget payload. Selection follows Card Sorting: the fill does NOT move, a 1.5px border-focus edge and a check in the same blue carry the state — which also keeps selection (an edge) and hover (a fill) on different channels by construction.

items.name: static-rendering
items.description: Agent skill: using @bydiorama/ui in Astro, SSR and static-export apps — which components are static-safe, which need a client:* directive, why compound components cannot be composed from .astro files and the wrapper pattern that fixes it, and the install traps (prettier, focus styles, paths outside src/ui). Issue #34.

items.name: ui-craft
items.description: Agent skill: the craft rules for building interfaces with @bydiorama/ui — radii, elevation, motion, icons, hit areas, colour usage. Install so coding agents in your app apply the same polish standards as the design system itself. Adapted from jakubkrehel/skills (MIT), see CREDITS.md.

items.name: effects
items.description: Agent skill: applying the effects layer in a consumer app (ADR 0022) — glass, grain, sheen, glow, shimmer and ink from `fx`, and the optional aurora and halo shaders from `shader`: the class-on-the-root pattern, setup order (@layer fx after Tailwind and the theme; startShaders() once), which effect for which job, what the layer already guarantees (per-brand glass tint, per-pixel contrast guard, reduced motion/transparency, forced colours) and the traps already paid for (refraction, halo clipping, sheen on pale accents, iOS canvas clipping).
